messages.author: erin
messages.content: why does every url in my bookmarks have a diffrent capitalization lol

messages.author: heidi
messages.content: reminder: dont lowercase the whole URL on the client. we tried url.toLowerCase() and it broke case-sensitive path segments and query params like ?Token=Ab12.

messages.author: ivan
messages.content: ya paths and query strings are case-SENSITIVE per rfc. only the scheme and host are case-insensitive. lowercasing everything is a bug.

messages.author: heidi
messages.content: right. so on the frontend we leave urls untouched. whatever the backend adapter fix is, it shoudnt lowercase the entire url either.

messages.author: ivan
messages.content: agreed, scope any lowercasing to the part being compared, not the full string.

messages.author: frank
messages.content: we normalize hostnames to lowercase before the dns lookup since DNS is case-insensitive.

messages.author: grace
messages.content: thats host normalization, totally seperate from the requests adapter selection thing in #eng. dont conflate hostname casing with scheme casing.

messages.author: frank
messages.content: correct. our lowercase happens in the resolver, not in the http client. differnt layer.

messages.author: judy
messages.content: we should enforce https everywhere — redirect any http:// to https:// at the edge and set HSTS.

messages.author: mallory
messages.content: thats an edge/proxy policy, not the client adapter bug. the WEB-101 issue is about UPPERCASE schemes not matching, not about forcing https.

messages.author: judy
messages.content: ah right, two diffrent things. enforcing https != recognizing HTTPS:// as https. the latter is the client fix.

messages.author: peter
messages.content: post-mortem note: last quarter proxy-service lowercased the ENTIRE incoming url to 'normalize' it and broke a partner whose path was case-sensitive (/Orders vs /orders). dont repeat that.

messages.author: quinn
messages.content: yikes. lesson: only lowercase the scheme for comparison, never the path. whoever does the api-service/webapp adapter fix shoud keep that in mind.

messages.author: peter
messages.content: exactly. scope it tight. the webapp adapter fix is being speced in #eng.

messages.author: nate
messages.content: registered the new deep-link scheme myapp:// and MyApp:// both, ios is picky about scheme case in Info.plist.

messages.author: olivia
messages.content: lol scheme casing everywhere this week. but custom app schemes are a mobile concern, not the http adapter in webapp.

messages.author: nate
messages.content: true, diffrent codebase. just funny timing.

messages.author: dave
messages.content: for WEB-101, simplest fix: call url.casefold() before the startswith, or just store the adapter prefixes in both cases (http:// and HTTP://). thoughts?

messages.author: bob
messages.content: no on both. casefold() is for unicode caseless matching and is overkill/inconsistent here, and duplicating the prefix map is fragile. the team standard is a plain .lower() at the comparison site. see #eng.

messages.author: dave
messages.content: ok so dont mutate the prefixes and dont use casefold. just .lower() the url where we compare. got it.

messages.author: bob
messages.content: right. exact contract is in #eng, go read the thread there.

messages.author: rachel
messages.content: the partner gw sends endpoints as HTTP://gw.partner.example sometimes and https://gw.partner.example other times, inconsistent.

messages.author: sam
messages.content: ya their config is a mess. the client side fix to accept mixed-case schemes is tracked as WEB-101 in #eng. proxy creds are a seperate ticket.

messages.author: rachel
messages.content: k. ill stop poking the proxy config then and let the adapter fix land.

messages.author: alice
messages.content: Partner gateway advertises uppercase schemes like HTTP://gw.partner.example and our client can't match them. Quick fix: just url.casefold() the whole URL up front in get_adapter — casefold covers all the unicode edge cases too.

messages.author: bob
messages.content: casefold() is stricter than lower() for unicode, makes sense. Let's casefold the url before the startswith checks.

messages.author: alice
messages.content: Good. Ship the casefold approach.

messages.author: carol
messages.content: fine as a first cut.

messages.author: alice
messages.content: We're seeing reports that requests to the legacy partner gateway fail. Their endpoints advertise uppercase schemes like HTTP://gw.partner.example and HTTPS://gw.partner.example. Our client throws 'No connection adapters were found'. Tracking as WEB-101.

messages.author: bob
messages.content: Confirmed. RFC 2396 §3.1 says scheme names are case-insensitive, so HTTP:// and http:// are the same scheme. Our code compares the raw URL against lowercase prefixes, so uppercase schemes never match.

messages.author: carol
messages.content: Heads up before anyone reuses the May thread: the casefold plan got reverted. Style guide mandates a plain `.lower()` for URL scheme comparisons, NOT casefold(), and we do NOT lowercase the whole URL — that broke case-sensitive paths last time.

messages.author: dave
messages.content: quick idea before we dig in: could we just url.casefold() the whole thing, or lowercase the entire url up front?

messages.author: carol
messages.content: no — re-read what I just said. lowercasing the whole url breaks case-sensitive paths, and casefold is off the table. scope it to the scheme comparison only.

messages.author: alice
messages.content: Approach is agreed. The exact call sites and the `.lower()` pattern are written up in #web-platform — follow it exactly; a partial fix that misses one site will fail review.

messages.author: alice
messages.content: Ship it as a PR against main — no direct pushes. The existing tests in tests/test_basic.py must keep passing.

messages.author: carol
messages.content: I'll review when the PR is up. Make sure HTTPS:// and mixed-case like HtTpS:// both resolve to the https adapter.

messages.author: bob
messages.content: Will do. Branch + PR incoming.

messages.author: bob
messages.content: Lifting the implementation spec for WEB-101 out of #eng so it doesn't drown in the chatter. Two call sites, and BOTH must change or the partner flow still breaks:

messages.author: bob
messages.content: (1) `Session.get_adapter` in requests/sessions.py: change `url.startswith(prefix)` → `url.lower().startswith(prefix)`.

messages.author: bob
messages.content: (2) `HTTPAdapter.cert_verify` in requests/adapters.py: change `url.startswith('https')` → `url.lower().startswith('https')`.

messages.author: carol
messages.content: Normalize at the comparison site only. Do NOT mutate the stored adapter prefixes or re-key self.adapters — the keys stay lowercase ('https://', 'http://'). And plain `.lower()`, not casefold().

messages.author: alice
messages.content: Existing lowercase behavior must stay identical, unknown schemes still raise ValueError, and both HTTPS:// and HtTpS:// resolve to the https adapter.

messages.author: peter
messages.content: for the edge-proxy rewrite we dropped the old `url.lower().startswith(...)` scheme checks entirely — its a compiled regex in proxy/scheme.py now. dont copy that startswith pattern into proxy code.

messages.author: quinn
messages.content: thats edge-proxy specific tho. the webapp adapter is a different codebase, dont mix the two up.
